{{Use mdy dates|date=May 2025}}
[[File:Al Arbour 1977.jpg|right|thumb|200px|[[Al Arbour]] led the Islanders to four consecutives [[Stanley Cup]]s from 1980 to 1983]]
The [[New York Islanders]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Elmont, New York]]. They play in the [[Metropolitan Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). The team joined the NHL in 1972, and won their first [[Stanley Cup]] championship in 1980. The Islanders play their home games at [[UBS Arena]] in Elmont.<ref name="Islanders">{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/islanders/ |title=New York Islanders |access-date=2008-06-07 |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |archive-date=2009-01-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090116224959/http://islanders.nhl.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Jon Ledecky]] and [[Scott D. Malkin]] are the Islanders' majority owners, [[Mathieu Darche]] is their [[general manager]], [[Peter DeBoer]] is the head coach and [[Anders Lee]] is the [[Captain (hockey)|team captain]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Roy fired as Islanders coach, replaced by DeBoer |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/patrick-roy-fired-as-new-york-islanders-coach-replaced-by-peter-deboer |website=NHL.com |access-date=April 5, 2026 |date=April 5, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/islanders/roster|title=Players|publisher=[[New York Islanders]]|access-date=2024-01-21|archive-date=2024-01-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117024013/https://www.nhl.com/islanders/roster|url-status=live}}</ref>

There have been 19 head coaches for the Islanders franchise. The team's first head coach was [[Phil Goyette]], who coached the team for part of the [[1972–73 NHL season|1972–73 season]].<ref name="Goyette"/> [[Al Arbour]] is the franchise's all-time leader for the most regular season games coached (1,500) and the most regular season game wins (740); he is also the franchise's all-time leader for the most playoff games coached (198), and the most playoff game wins (119).<ref name="Arbour">{{cite web |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/arboual01c.html |title=Al Arbour |access-date=2008-06-05 |publisher=Sports Reference, LLC |work=Hockey-Reference |archive-date=2008-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080807170628/http://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/arboual01c.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Arbour is the only Islanders coach to have been inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.<ref name="Arbour"/> He and Trotz are the only Islanders coaches to have won the [[Jack Adams Award]] as the NHL's top coach.<ref name="Arbour"/> The franchise has participated in the [[Stanley Cup Final]] five times, coached by Arbour each time; they won [[Stanley Cup]] four of those times. Arbour, [[Terry Simpson]], [[Peter Laviolette]], [[Steve Stirling]], [[Ted Nolan]], [[Jack Capuano]], [[Barry Trotz]], [[Lane Lambert]], and [[Patrick Roy]] are the coaches who coached the team into the Stanley Cup playoffs.<ref name="Arbour"/><ref name="Simpson"/><ref name="Laviolette"/><ref name="Stirling"/><ref name="Nolan">{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/nolante01c.html|title=Ted Nolan|access-date=2008-06-05|publisher=Sports Reference, LLC|work=Hockey-Reference|archive-date=2008-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820033859/http://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/nolante01c.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Notes==
* {{note label|Note1|a|a}} A running total of the number of coaches of the Islanders. Thus, any coach who has two or more separate terms as head coach is only counted once.
* {{note label|Note2|b|b}} Before the 2005–06 season, the NHL instituted a [[Overtime (ice hockey)#Shootout|penalty shootout]] for regular season games that remained tied after a five-minute overtime period, which prevented ties.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511234846/http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|archive-date=2008-05-11|title=Official Rules|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|access-date=2008-12-05}}</ref>
* {{note label|Note3|c|c}} In hockey, the winning percentage is calculated by dividing points by maximum possible [[Point (ice hockey)|points]].
* {{note label|Note4|d|d}} Each year is linked to an article about that particular NHL season.
* {{note label|Note5|e|e}} Arbour replaced Ted Nolan as an interim head coach for one game in order to have coached 1500 Islanders games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://islanders.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=334735|title=Al Arbour returns to coach 1500th game|date=2007-07-19|publisher=[[New York Islanders]]|access-date=2009-01-20|archive-date=2008-04-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080421114849/http://islanders.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=334735|url-status=dead}}</ref>
